name: Crypto stress
summary: Record $6.3bn hack at Binance; withdrawals reopening, Bitcoin 10% off its high
state: Attackers drained about $6.3bn from Binance, the largest exchange, in late October; deposits and withdrawals were suspended and began reopening in phases on 1 Nov. The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea on 1 Nov. Binance says 95% of the loss is covered and promises proof of reserves by 3 Nov. Bitcoin was near $78,000, about 10% below its high.
for_you: Customers of Binance may face delays on some withdrawals while assets return in phases. A shortfall in reserves would matter most for those holding funds on the exchange; the 3 Nov reserves report is the next marker.
rubric_hit: Top-10 exchange under stress (Binance $6.3bn hack, withdrawals suspended) = Watch; BTC drawdown 10% < 25%

sources.title: TechCrunch — North Korean hackers blamed for stealing record $6.3B in Binance breach
Tech-ish — FBI says North Korea stole more than $6 billion from Binance as withdrawals reopen

why: Crypto is now plumbed into mainstream finance via ETFs and stablecoins; a crash or de-peg can spill into funding markets.
drivers: Liquidity, leverage, regulation, stablecoin reserves, exchange solvency.

rubric.alert: Drawdown > 45%, or a major stablecoin de-pegs (> 3% for > 24h), or a top-10 exchange fails.
rubric.watch: Drawdown 25–45%, or a top-10 exchange/stablecoin under stress.
rubric.normal: Bitcoin drawdown from 52-week high < 25% and no major stablecoin/exchange incidents.
